chapter: Cincinnati, Buffalo, Russell and Fletcher Henderson
title: How Dixieland and ragtime bands are put together
summary: He explains that the trumpet leads and everyone else keeps off each other; Red Allen taught him Dixieland tunes.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: How would you describe, in your words, the difference between the Dixieland music and the ragtime?
That's just about impossible.
I mean, if you played in a ragtime band, how would -
They mostly used trombones for slide, you know.
For ragtime?
Dixieland and ragtime, yeah.
What were the other instruments playing? Who was playing the melody line?
Who was playing the melody? On these tunes? Red Allen.
No, in a Dixieland orchestration, the makeup of the band.
The trumpet player usually played. ... (SINGS)...

It doesn't take long because even now I could bring a tune out here if I had my chops and play any kind of tune I ever heard. All you have to do is fill in, listen, and fill in in the right time and right place. Dixieland tunes, they have special notes, but Red would teach me, you know, during intermission, take me upstairs and tell me. I mean, it wouldn't be hard to remember because when you hear something ... all you have to do is fill in and play correct chords... That's the way I learned to play Dixieland.
You say before that you were playing jazz?
Real jazz music, yeah.
What were the other instruments, like you said the trumpet player played the lead and the trombone played their part. What was the clarinet and the saxophone and the others doing?
Say it again.
What other - what melodic lines did the other instruments play?
I don't know - they were playing their own stuff. They know how to keep off each other. When you know a tune, you know
how to keep off each other. It's like three of you would start singing a tune now and if all three of you knew it, you knew what part to sing. Like that.
They would know the harmonic part to play?
No, just keep off each other.
